_about: Manifest of ODBC drivers under stress-test. Single source of truth for (a) the version of each driver to install in CI, (b) the URL/apt package to install it from, and (c) the upstream git repo + tag whose source matches that binary version. Consumed by .github/workflows/stress-test.yml at runtime via `jq` and by the /triage-driver skill at analysis time. apt_version strings are formatted for `apt-get install pkg=version`; if Ubuntu drops a pinned version from its repos the workflow will fail loudly at the install step and this file must be updated. The `version` field is the upstream form (what SQLGetInfo reports); apt_version is the Debian-formatted form. Firebird is included as of v3.5.0-rc1 (the first release of the refactored driver). H11 adds a `provenance` block per driver, read only by the triage skill: it declares whether actual_version.txt is a real observation or an echo of this file, and whether SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) can be trusted. Without it the skill's version cross-check compared the manifest against itself for three drivers and could not fail. Purely additive - the workflow does not read it. H17 adds `firebird-official` / `firebird-patched`, the manifest's first *pair*: the same server, the same connection string and the same crusher binary against two builds of one driver, so the diff between their two reports isolates the driver. They are Windows entries because the official 3.0.x line has no Linux binary. An `install.sha256` appears on those two: the version resource cannot distinguish a prerelease rebuild, so the digest is what pins the artifact. T4 adds an optional `pair_with` key naming another driver in this manifest that the entry is meant to be compared against; triage.ps1 and fetch-stress-test.ps1 enforce the two conditions that comparison rests on. U2 adds `firebird-official-linux` / `firebird-patched-linux`, a second pair on Linux, where the two Linux-only defects among the seventeen live. `install.method: build_from_source` appears there for the first time: no Linux binary of 3.0.1.21 was ever published, so CI compiles the pinned commit instead of downloading anything, and the entry carries no `install.sha256` because the commit is the pin.

provenance._note: actual_version.txt carries `dpkg -s odbc-postgresql | awk '/^Version:/'`, which is a genuine observation of what got installed. Debian form (epoch `1:`, revision `-1`) differs from the upstream `version` field; the triage comparer normalises both before matching.
Same as postgresql: actual_version.txt comes from `dpkg -s odbc-mariadb`, and the job fails loudly if it disagrees with apt_version.

actual_version.txt is parsed out of the extracted `mysql-connector-odbc-<version>-linux-*` directory name, so it reflects the tarball that was actually unpacked rather than the URL that was requested.

H11. Both halves of the provenance cross-check are unusable for this driver, and saying so is the point of this block. (a) The job has no version string to extract from the bare .so, so it echoes this file's `version` into actual_version.txt - comparing the two therefore compares the manifest with itself and can never fail. (b) DuckDB answers SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) with `03.51.0000`, its ODBC *compliance level*, not its product version, so driver_info.driver_version is no help either. Triage reports this as PROVENANCE=UNVERIFIABLE rather than a false OK. Use SQL_DBMS_VER if you need a real number at runtime.

duckdb._conn_string_note: H15: `Database=` is required, not optional. Without it the driver falls back to IN_MEMORY_PATH (`:memory:`) at connect.cpp:148, and connect.cpp:187 sets `cache_instance = database != IN_MEMORY_PATH` — false — so every SQLConnect gets its *own* database object. Five probes that create a table on the primary connection and read it from a sibling therefore could not pass against any driver, and the catalog probes saw an empty schema. Keys are lowercased at connect.cpp:56, so the `Database=` spelling matches. A file also persists across the two crusher invocations the run-crusher action makes; that is safe because RoundTripTableGuard reuses and empties a pre-existing table (A15), which is the same situation the postgres/mysql jobs are already in.

install._note: Server brought up via ClickHouse's own deb repo; server version is not part of the triage contract — only the driver version is pinned.

provenance._note: H11. The job echoes this file's `version` into actual_version.txt, so that comparison is the manifest against itself. driver_info.driver_version is believed usable here (unlike duckdb/firebird), so triage falls back to it as the one genuinely observed value.

install._note: Server brought up via PSFirebird (Firebird 5.0.3); the .tar.gz ships only libOdbcFb.so + odbcinst.ini.sample, registered manually.

provenance._note: H11. Same shape as duckdb, found the same way - by reading a stored artifact. The .tar.gz carries no extractable version, so actual_version.txt is an echo of this file's `version`; and the driver answers SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) with `00.00.000`, which is why the old skill's cross-check passed a driver that reported no version at all. PROVENANCE=UNVERIFIABLE is the honest answer until the driver reports a real version or CI observes one.

firebird-official._pair_note: T4. The other half of the H17 pair. The pair's whole method is 'two runs differing in the driver and nothing else', and the two conditions that rests on - an identical connection string, and the same crusher binary - used to be true only by convention. triage.ps1 now reads this key, checks the two entries name each other, refuses to proceed if their conn_string differs by one character, and compares the two reports' `environment` blocks when the sibling has already been triaged. fetch-stress-test.ps1 reads it too: asking for one half brings the other along and prints the report diff. See also stress-test.yml's `firebird-pair` selector (T3), which is the same guarantee on the CI side.

install._note: H17. Windows by necessity, not by preference: the official 3.0.x line ships as Inno Setup installers and the repack publishes exactly two assets per tag (Win32 + x64 .exe). There is no Linux .so for this build, so the existing linux `firebird` job could not have run it. Installed with `/VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`; the default setup type is DeveloperInstall, the one that drops FirebirdODBC.dll in System32 and self-registers it - Install/Win32/OdbcJdbcSetup.iss marks the file `Flags: regserver`, so registration happens inside the DLL's DllRegisterServer and there is no [Registry] section to read the driver name from. `driver_section` is what that registration writes: OdbcJdbcSetup/Setup.cpp:249 passes DRIVER_FULL_NAME, which SetupAttributes.h:39 defines as "Firebird ODBC Driver" - the same name the v3.5.x WiX installer uses, which is why this entry and firebird-patched can share one connection string verbatim.

source._note: H17. A commit, not a tag, because upstream never tagged this build. The 3.0.x line keeps its build number in WriteBuildNo.h, and dee624f ("Issue #270 : Fix incorrect behavior, buildno++ (21)", 2026-01-16) is the commit that set BUILDNUM_VERSION to 21; the next bump (8e64f5e, 2026-03-31) goes to 22, and the repack published these installers on 2026-01-22, so the whole 21 window is dee624f..8e64f5e^. The nearest real tag, v3-0-1-release, is build 18 - it would have pointed triage at source three builds older than the binary it is explaining. triage.ps1 accepts a 40-hex SHA here and fetches it by object id.

provenance._note: H17. The first Firebird entry whose actual_version.txt is a genuine observation rather than an echo of this file. On Windows the installed System32\FirebirdODBC.dll carries a VERSIONINFO resource and the job reads its ProductVersion back out after the installer runs - "3.0.1.21", which is exactly the string to compare. The download is separately gated on the sha256 above, so a re-cut release asset fails the job instead of being triaged as this build. SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) stays unusable for the reason recorded on the `firebird` entry.

firebird-official._conn_string_note: Deliberately identical to firebird-patched's, character for character, so that any difference between the two reports is the driver and not the configuration - that comparison is the entire point of the pair. Forward slashes in the Windows path are also deliberate: Firebird accepts them (verified against a live 5.0.3 through this same driver name), and they keep the string free of backslashes that would otherwise have to survive JSON, $GITHUB_ENV and a bash double-quoted argument unscathed.

firebird-patched._pair_note: T4. The other half of the H17 pair. The pair's whole method is 'two runs differing in the driver and nothing else', and the two conditions that rests on - an identical connection string, and the same crusher binary - used to be true only by convention. triage.ps1 now reads this key, checks the two entries name each other, refuses to proceed if their conn_string differs by one character, and compares the two reports' `environment` blocks when the sibling has already been triaged. fetch-stress-test.ps1 reads it too: asking for one half brings the other along and prints the report diff. See also stress-test.yml's `firebird-pair` selector (T3), which is the same guarantee on the CI side.

install._note: H17. The MSI rather than the .zip, so the driver is registered by the same route a user takes; installer/Product.wxs defines DriverName as "Firebird ODBC Driver" and writes the ODBCINST.INI keys itself. `msiexec /i <msi> /qn /norestart`. The x64 MSI also registers the 32-bit driver for WoW64, which is irrelevant here - crusher is x64 - but harmless.

source._note: H17. fdcastel's fork, not FirebirdSQL's: this is an unofficial build, upstream `master` @ 35fae3e with thirteen open pull requests merged on top, and only the fork carries the tag. The release notes enumerate the thirteen; they are the fixes this pair exists to measure.

provenance._note: H17. actual_version.txt is the installed DLL's ProductVersion, a real observation - but it reads "3.5.1.0", because the MSI drops the prerelease suffix (the release notes say so, and warn that rc1 must be uninstalled first for exactly this reason). So the version resource cannot tell rc1 from rc2 and the sha256 gate is what does; the version comparison here can only confirm the 3.5.1 line. triage.ps1's ConvertTo-VersionParts strips the `-rc2` suffix so this reads MATCH rather than a spurious MISMATCH.

firebird-patched._conn_string_note: See firebird-official's note - the two are identical on purpose. Both installers register the driver under the same name, so the two jobs cannot run on one machine, which is why they are separate jobs and not a matrix over one.

firebird-official-linux.display_name: Firebird ODBC Driver 3.0.1.21 (official, built from source) on Linux
firebird-official-linux._pair_note: U2. The Linux half of the H17 pair, and the reason it took a second pass: the Windows pair cannot see the Linux-only defects among the seventeen - #288's ConvertingString heap overflow on the widechar path, and #316 item 6, where SQLColAttribute was exported under its C++ mangled name so the driver manager could not find it and routed every call through the ODBC 2 entry point. Neither exists on Windows, where the .def file names the exports. **This pair is asymmetric in how each binary is obtained, and that is a real caveat**: the patched half is the published Linux x64 tarball pinned by sha256, and the official half is built from its pinned commit in CI because no Linux binary of 3.0.1.21 was ever published. So the two are not guaranteed to share compiler flags the way the Windows pair shares an installer format. A difference between them is still evidence, but it is one step weaker than the Windows pair's, and a finding that turns on optimisation or hardening rather than driver logic would be indistinguishable here.

install._note: U2. There is no published Linux binary of 3.0.1.21 to download, and the nearest one - linux_libs.zip at v3-0-1-release - is build 18, not 21. Comparing a build-18 binary against build-21 source is exactly the confusion install.sha256 exists to prevent, so this entry carries no sha256 and is not weaker for it: CI clones source.tag and builds it in the same run, which proves directly the thing a digest can only assert. A from-source build is not byte-reproducible anyway - paths, timestamps and compiler point releases all move it - so a pinned digest here would have to be re-cut every time the runner image changed and would pin nothing in between. The build is what upstream documents in Builds/Gcc.lin/readme.linux: unixodbc-dev, rename makefile.linux, make. The Firebird client headers are vendored in the tree, so no Firebird development package is needed.

provenance._note: U2. The strongest provenance in this manifest, and it needed its own version_source because it is not shaped like the others. There is no downloaded artifact to digest: the binary is compiled from source.tag in the same workflow run, so "is this binary that source" is answered by construction rather than by comparison. actual_version.txt carries the version the *source tree itself* declares - MAJOR_VERSION, MINOR_VERSION and REVNO_VERSION from SetupAttributes.h with BUILDNUM_VERSION from WriteBuildNo.h, the same four constants the upstream makefile reads to name its own package - so a MISMATCH here means the manifest pins a version the pinned commit does not declare, which is a real manifest bug rather than an artefact. At dee624f those constants read 3, 0, 1 and 21. SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) stays unusable for the reason recorded on the `firebird` entry.

firebird-patched-linux.display_name: Firebird ODBC Driver 3.5.1-rc2 (master + 13 PRs) on Linux
firebird-patched-linux._pair_note: U2. The Linux half of the H17 pair, and the reason it took a second pass: the Windows pair cannot see the Linux-only defects among the seventeen - #288's ConvertingString heap overflow on the widechar path, and #316 item 6, where SQLColAttribute was exported under its C++ mangled name so the driver manager could not find it and routed every call through the ODBC 2 entry point. Neither exists on Windows, where the .def file names the exports. **This pair is asymmetric in how each binary is obtained, and that is a real caveat**: the patched half is the published Linux x64 tarball pinned by sha256, and the official half is built from its pinned commit in CI because no Linux binary of 3.0.1.21 was ever published. So the two are not guaranteed to share compiler flags the way the Windows pair shares an installer format. A difference between them is still evidence, but it is one step weaker than the Windows pair's, and a finding that turns on optimisation or hardening rather than driver logic would be indistinguishable here.

install._note: U2. Downloaded rather than built, unlike its pair. The 3.5.x line publishes a Linux x64 tarball, so the released artifact is available and pinning it by digest is the strongest claim that can be made about a binary somebody else compiled. Building this half from source too would have made the pair symmetric, and was rejected: the 3.5.x tree builds with CMake whose version comes from `git describe`, so it needs full history rather than the single pinned object, and its own CI runs an install-prerequisites step before configuring. Two more moving parts on the half that already has a published binary. The asymmetry is recorded in _pair_note rather than smoothed over. The tarball ships only libOdbcFb.so and odbcinst.ini.sample, registered manually - same as the `firebird` entry.

provenance._note: U2. The .so carries no version resource the way a Windows DLL does, and the tarball has no version string that can be extracted reliably, so actual_version.txt echoes this file - the same convention the duckdb, clickhouse and `firebird` entries use, and it proves nothing. Binary identity here rests entirely on install.sha256. That is a weaker claim than its pair's build-from-source, which is the asymmetry _pair_note records.

install._note: F8: this said method 'release_asset' with a releases/latest URL, while stress-test.yml has always downloaded the artifact from the most recent successful master ci.yml run - so the manifest sent readers to a route nothing takes, which matters because this file is the source of truth the /triage-driver skill reads. Using CI is deliberate: it closes the release-cadence gap, so a stress-test run exercises the driver as it is now rather than as it was at the last tag. Mock driver is built from this repo; for triage the 'source' is the workspace itself, not a remote clone.
install._release_asset_note: What a *user* installs, and it does exist - kept for that reason, not used by CI. release.yml publishes this for Windows only, though ci.yml now builds the mock on all three platforms.

source._note: Triage skill special-cases mock-driver — no clone step, points at this repo's mock-driver/ directory directly.

provenance._note: H11. `version` is the literal string "workspace"; actual_version.txt carries the 12-char short SHA of the master CI run the binary came from. There is no version to cross-check, so triage skips the comparison and records the SHA as the workspace state to diff against.
